gaps.title: Complete closure requires every named issuer authority class
gaps.close_criteria: A complete bundle may contain multiple submissions for one gap and is eligible only when every authority class listed by the canonical contract is represented by a cryptographically valid submission. Within one gap, authority seats use distinct trust-registry key IDs and distinct identity/organization pairs. Across the complete package, one key ID and one identity/organization pair may be reused only for the same narrowly scoped authority class; one omnipotent key or identity cannot fill unrelated roles merely because they occur in different gaps. Same-class reuse across related gaps remains permitted and tested. Partial or aliased bundles never produce all_authority_owned_gaps_closed=true.

gaps.title: Final signed review roster and acceptance context are removal-resistant
gaps.close_criteria: Every accepted bundle requires every final signed review artifact to carry the same schema-v1 G10 closure manifest. The manifest binds the explicit policy ID/revision, ordered final reviewer roster, acceptance state, reviewed_at, decision_reference and limitations. Because each review artifact digest is in the reviewer Ed25519 statement, removing, adding, replacing or reordering a final reviewer, changing final acceptance context, or substituting another policy revision fails validation. External governance still determines whether every accountable review was admitted to the final roster.

gaps.title: Complete-closure semantics are versioned and issuer claims are authority-scoped
gaps.close_criteria: The canonical external-evidence contract revision is 2026-09-02-g10-quorum-1 and explicitly identifies its G9 predecessor, all-class quorum mode, exact class-scoped claim mode, distinct authority seats and review-manifest profile. Required claims are a validated disjoint partition across the named authority classes for each gap. Each issuer may sign exactly its assigned claims; missing or cross-scope claims fail before acceptance. Contract revision is inside issuer and reviewer signature preimages, and policy ID/revision are inside review-set and acceptance-context digests, so a G10 package cannot be accepted by the older G9 semantic revision. The policy module itself, the acceptance-module alias, the CLI and the package-level validator all resolve to the same immutable, aggregate-bounded validation-snapshot entrypoint; explicitly importing complete_closure cannot bypass filesystem custody.

gaps.title: Repository CI discovers every committed accepted immutable successor
gaps.close_criteria: Repository qualification recursively inspects bounded regular files under evidence/external by canonical envelope content rather than only matching a top-level bundle.json filename. The authoritative scanner opens the root from the filesystem anchor and traverses every child through no-follow directory descriptors. Lexical, opened and post-traversal directory identities and lexical, opened and post-read file identities must agree. Symbolic links, special objects, ordinary file or parent-directory replacement, unstable reads, oversized files, excessive aggregate bytes, excessive entries, excessive depth and unsupported no-follow APIs fail the gate rather than being ignored. Every discovered envelope whose contract_id is canonical and acceptance.state is accepted is revalidated as complete and accepted under a protected out-of-band trust-registry pin. Filename, extension, nesting, successor placement or ancestor replacement cannot hide or inject an accepted package.

gaps.title: Authority-bearing validation cannot inherit caller clock or executable authority
gaps.close_criteria: The supported package API, direct complete_closure module, package-name compatibility import, verifier CLI and signing path use the trusted current system clock and only the absolute /usr/bin/openssl executable. Every path ancestor and the executable must be a real root-owned, non-group/world-writable object; the executable is opened with no-follow semantics and its lexical/opened/post-check identity must agree. Cryptographic subprocesses run under a minimal deterministic environment and do not inherit caller PATH, OPENSSL_CONF, OPENSSL_MODULES, LD_PRELOAD, DYLD injection variables or another environment override. Caller-supplied validation time, custom executable, shell execution, subprocess executable replacement and caller environment are rejected before cryptographic use. The CLI exposes no cryptographic-binary override. The deterministic underscored clock hook is test-only and not a sandbox against arbitrary code already executing inside the trusted verifier process. Hostile tests prove a same-name attacker program placed first on PATH is not executed for private-key validation, signing or verification.

gaps.title: Issuer and reviewer signatures bind canonical contract semantics
gaps.close_criteria: Every issuer and reviewer canonical Ed25519 preimage contains a contract-binding statement with contract ID, declared revision and the canonical SHA-256 of the complete current contract object. The evidence-set digest carries the same binding. A contract whose revision string is unchanged but whose authority classes, claim partition, review rules, closure rule or any other canonical field changes produces different submission, evidence-set and review digests and invalidates existing signatures. A caller-supplied revision that differs from the current contract bytes fails before signing or verification.
